source.text: Καὶ εὐθέως ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι εἰς πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν, ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately he compelled the disciples to get into a boat and to go before him to the other side, until he should dismiss the crowds.

en.L: And immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the other side, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dismissed the crowds.
en.B: Straight after this, Jesus insisted that the disciples get into the boat and go on before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} across the lake. Meanwhile {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would send the crowds home.
en.R: Right after that, Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to get into the boat. He made them go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the other side of the lake. He stayed behind to send the people home.

es.L: Y enseguida obligó a los discípulos a embarcarse e ir por delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a la otra orilla, hasta que despidiera a las multitudes.
es.B: Inmediatamente después, Jesús insistió en que los discípulos subieran a la barca y cruzaran el lago antes que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Mientras tanto, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} despediría a la gente.
es.R: Enseguida, Jesús les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores que subieran a la barca. Hizo que se adelantaran al otro lado del lago. Él se quedó para mandar a la gente a sus casas.

fr.L: Et aussitôt {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} obligea les disciples à monter dans la barque et à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} précéder sur l’autre rive, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ait renvoyé les foules.
fr.B: Aussitôt après, Jésus pressa les disciples de monter dans la barque et de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} précéder de l’autre côté du lac. Pendant ce temps, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait renvoyer les foules chez elles.
fr.R: Juste après, Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de monter dans le bateau. Il les a obligés à partir avant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de l’autre côté du lac. Il est resté pour renvoyer les gens chez eux.

sw.L: Na mara moja akawashurutisha wanafunzi kupanda mashua na kwenda mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hadi upande wa pili, hadi atakapokuwa amewaruhusu umati kuondoka.
sw.B: Mara baada ya hayo, Yesu aliwasisitiza wanafunzi wapande mashua na kumtangulia kuvuka ziwa. Wakati huo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} angewaaga watu waende nyumbani.
sw.R: Mara moja Yesu aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waingie katika mashua. Aliwafanya watangulie kwenda upande wa pili wa ziwa. Yeye alibaki nyuma ili kuwaaga watu waende nyumbani.

vi.L: Và lập tức {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt các môn đồ xuống thuyền và đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua bờ bên kia, trong khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giải tán đoàn dân.
vi.B: Ngay sau đó, Đức Giê-xu giục các môn đồ xuống thuyền và qua bờ bên kia trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, trong khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho dân chúng ra về.
vi.R: Ngay sau đó, Đức Giê-xu bảo các môn đồ xuống thuyền. Ngài bắt họ đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua bên kia hồ. Ngài ở lại để cho dân chúng về nhà.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 그분이 제자들을 재촉하여 배에 오르게 하시고, 자기가 무리를 보내시는 동안 자기보다 먼저 건너편으로 가게 하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 곧바로 제자들을 재촉하여 배에 태우시고 자기보다 먼저 건너편으로 가게 하셨다. 그동안 무리를 돌려보내려고 하셨다.
ko.R: 그 일이 있은 뒤에 예수께서는 바로 제자들에게 배를 타라고 하셨다. 그리고 자기보다 먼저 호수 건너편으로 가게 하셨다. 예수께서는 남아서 사람들을 집으로 돌려보내셨다.

am.L: ወዲያውም ሕዝቡን እስኪያሰናብት ድረስ ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ወደ ጀልባ ገብተው ወደ ማዶ ቀድመውት እንዲሄዱ አስገደዳቸው።
am.B: ከዚህ በኋላ ወዲያውኑ ኢየሱስ ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ወደ ጀልባዋ ገብተው ቀድመውት ሐይቁን እንዲሻገሩ አጥብቆ አዘዛቸው። እርሱ እስከዚያው ሕዝቡን ወደየቤታቸው ያሰናብት ነበር።
am.R: ከዚያ በኋላ ወዲያው ኢየሱስ ደቀ መዛሙርቱን ወደ ጀልባዋ እንዲገቡ ነገራቸው። ቀድመውት ወደ ሐይቁ ማዶ እንዲሄዱ አደረገ። እርሱ ግን ሕዝቡን ወደየቤታቸው ለመሸኘት ወደኋላ ቀረ።

decisions.choice: compelled: made them go, insisted
alternatives: forced them against their will by threat
decisions.reason: The verb is strong. Matthew does not say why Jesus sent them off so firmly. John 6:15 tells that the crowd wanted to make Jesus king.

decisions.choice: until he dismissed the crowds: while he sent the crowds away
alternatives: they were to wait for him to dismiss them
decisions.reason: The disciples are to leave at once, and Jesus will send the crowds away himself.

decisions.choice: the other side: across the lake
decisions.reason: They arrive at Gennesaret (14:34).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on separate pronouns and possessives only (él, lo, le, su, tú, ti)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("tráiganmelos"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English through the passage; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is capitalised either way and takes no span.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept at Literal (14:31)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 3) and Mark 6:45-56: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable tells the story in the passé composé. Speech keeps its own tenses. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "les disciples" (R)
decisions.reason: French keeps "disciples" at every level (style guide section 5), as Mark 6:45 does at Readable. The same holds in 14:26 and 14:34.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on free pronouns and possessives only (yake, yeye, wake, wewe, kwako, mimi)
decisions.reason: Swahili carries "he" and "him" in the verb, where a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers only free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the passage.

decisions.choice: "lập tức" (L); "ngay sau đó" (B, R); "bắt" (L), "giục" (B), "bảo ... bắt" (R) for "compelled"
decisions.reason: The wording of the parallel, Mark 6:45. "Lập tức" is the Literal word for "immediately" through the Gospels; "bắt" and "giục" keep the insistence of the Greek verb (meaning decision) without the force of "ép".

decisions.choice: "bờ bên kia" (L, B); "bên kia hồ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:45; Readable names the lake, the word it uses for the Sea of Galilee through 14:22-34.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in 해라체, people speak to him in 합쇼체, through Matthew 14:22-36
alternatives: Capitalised pronouns, which Korean does not have
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "곧" (L); "곧바로" (B); "바로" (R) for immediately; "재촉하여" (L, B) for compelled
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 6:45 and the Korean Gospels: one word per level for "immediately". He urged them strongly (meaning decision); "재촉하다" says that without suggesting force.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span in Amharic
alternatives: A span like the English one
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the English choice between "him" and "Him" has nothing to change in Amharic, and the Amharic text carries no deity_pronoun spans in this passage.

source.text: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατ’ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having dismissed the crowds he went up into the mountain by himself to pray.

en.L: And having dismissed the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on the mountain by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to pray.
en.B: Once the crowds had gone, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} climbed up into the hills by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to pray.
en.R: After the people left, Jesus went up on a hill by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to pray.

es.L: Y después de despedir a las multitudes, subió al monte a solas para orar.
es.B: Cuando la gente se hubo ido, subió a solas al monte para orar.
es.R: Cuando la gente se fue, Jesús subió solo a un monte para orar.

fr.L: Et après avoir renvoyé les foules, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta sur la montagne, à l’écart, pour prier.
fr.B: Une fois les foules parties, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta seul dans les collines pour prier.
fr.R: Quand les gens sont partis, Jésus est monté seul sur une colline pour prier.

sw.L: Na baada ya kuwaaga umati, akapanda mlimani peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ili aombe.
sw.B: Umati ulipokwisha kuondoka, alipanda vilimani peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ili aombe.
sw.R: Watu walipoondoka, Yesu alipanda kilimani peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ili aombe.

vi.L: Và sau khi giải tán đoàn dân, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi lên núi riêng một mình để cầu nguyện.
vi.B: Sau khi cho dân chúng về, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên vùng đồi một mình để cầu nguyện.
vi.R: Khi dân chúng đã về hết, Đức Giê-xu đi lên một ngọn đồi một mình để cầu nguyện.

ko.L: 그리고 무리를 보내신 뒤에, 그분은 기도하시려고 따로 산에 올라가셨다.
ko.B: 무리를 보내신 뒤에, 예수께서는 기도하시려고 혼자 산에 올라가셨다.
ko.R: 사람들이 떠난 뒤에, 예수께서는 기도하시려고 혼자 언덕에 올라가셨다.

am.L: ሕዝቡንም አሰናብቶ ሊጸልይ ብቻውን ወደ ተራራው ወጣ።
am.B: ሕዝቡ ከሄዱ በኋላ ሊጸልይ ብቻውን ወደ ኮረብቶቹ ወጣ።
am.R: ሰዎቹ ከሄዱ በኋላ ኢየሱስ ሊጸልይ ብቻውን ወደ አንድ ኮረብታ ወጣ።

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country by the lake
decisions.reason: The word means a mountain or the hills. The hills rise steeply from the lake of Galilee. Matthew often places Jesus on a mountain (5:1; 15:29; 17:1; 28:16).

decisions.choice: by himself to pray: Jesus seeks God alone
decisions.reason: Jesus had taught his disciples to pray in secret (6:6). He goes alone again to pray in Gethsemane (26:36-44).

decisions.choice: into the hills (B); on a hill (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the hill country without suggesting a high peak.

decisions.choice: el monte
decisions.reason: English says "hills" because "the mountain" suggests one peak. Spanish "monte" also covers hill country (meaning decision m1), so every level keeps it, as in John 6:3.

decisions.choice: "à l’écart" (L); "seul" (B, R)
decisions.reason: French says "by himself" with "à l’écart" or "seul", which carry no pronoun, so no deity_pronoun span is needed where English has one on "himself" (also 14:23b).

decisions.choice: "núi" (L); "vùng đồi" (B); "một ngọn đồi" (R)
decisions.reason: The mountain is the hill country by the lake (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek word, Balanced and Readable say hills, as Mark 6:46 does at Readable.
The mountain is the hill country by the lake (meaning decision); Readable uses the plainer "언덕", as the English Readable says "a hill".

source.text: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Evening now having come alone he was there.

en.L: And when evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was there alone.
en.B: Evening came, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still there by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.R: When it got dark, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was there alone.

es.L: Y al caer la noche, se encontraba allí solo.
es.B: Llegó la noche, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} seguía allí solo.

fr.L: Et le soir venu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était là seul.
fr.B: Le soir tomba, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était toujours là, seul.
fr.R: Quand la nuit est tombée, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était là, tout seul.

sw.B: Jioni ikaingia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alikuwa bado pale peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

vi.L: Và khi chiều tối đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đó một mình.
vi.B: Chiều tối đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn còn ở đó một mình.
vi.R: Khi trời tối, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn ở đó một mình.

ko.L: 저녁이 되었을 때, 그분은 거기에 혼자 계셨다.
ko.B: 저녁이 되었는데도, 예수께서는 아직 거기에 홀로 계셨다.
ko.R: 날이 어두워졌을 때에도 예수께서는 거기에 혼자 계셨다.

am.B: መሸ፤ እርሱም አሁንም በዚያ ብቻውን ነበር።

decisions.choice: evening: nightfall, after dark
decisions.reason: The same phrase as 14:15 marks a later point in the day. Hours have passed since the meal; the night is coming on.

decisions.choice: when it got dark
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this is later than the "evening" of 14:15.

source.text: τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν, βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος.

records.literal_gloss: And the boat already stadia many from the land was distant, being tormented by the waves, was for contrary the wind.

en.L: But the boat was already many stadia away from the land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against [it].
en.B: By then the boat was {{units:a mile or more|many stadia}} from shore, and the waves were pounding it, since the wind was blowing against them.
en.R: By this time the boat was far from land, {{units:a mile or more|many stadia}} out. The waves were beating hard against it, because the wind was blowing the wrong way.

es.L: Pero la barca distaba ya muchos estadios de la tierra, atormentada por las olas, pues el viento [le] era contrario.
es.B: Para entonces la barca estaba a {{units:dos kilómetros o más|muchos estadios}} de la orilla, y las olas la golpeaban, porque el viento soplaba en contra.
es.R: La barca ya estaba lejos de la tierra, a {{units:dos kilómetros o más|muchos estadios}}. Las olas la golpeaban con fuerza, porque el viento soplaba en contra.

fr.L: Or la barque était déjà à de nombreux stades de la terre, battue par les vagues, car le vent était contraire.
fr.B: La barque était alors à {{units:plus d’un kilomètre et demi|de nombreux stades}} du rivage, et les vagues la secouaient, car le vent soufflait contre eux.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, le bateau était loin de la terre, à {{units:plus d’un kilomètre et demi|de nombreux stades}}. Les vagues le frappaient fort, parce que le vent soufflait dans le mauvais sens.

sw.L: Lakini mashua ilikuwa tayari stadia nyingi mbali na nchi kavu, ikiteswa na mawimbi, kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa kinyume [nayo].
sw.B: Wakati huo mashua ilikuwa {{units:kilomita mbili au zaidi|stadia nyingi}} kutoka pwani, nayo mawimbi yakiipiga kwa nguvu, kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa ukivuma kuwaelekea.
sw.R: Wakati huo mashua ilikuwa mbali na nchi kavu, {{units:kilomita mbili au zaidi|stadia nyingi}} ndani ya ziwa. Mawimbi yaliipiga kwa nguvu, kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa ukivuma kutoka upande waliokuwa wakienda.

vi.L: Còn chiếc thuyền thì đã cách đất liền nhiều ếch-ta-đơ, bị sóng đánh vùi dập, vì gió ngược.
vi.B: Lúc ấy chiếc thuyền đã cách bờ {{units:vài cây số|nhiều ếch-ta-đơ}}, và bị sóng đánh dữ dội, vì gió thổi ngược.
vi.R: Lúc ấy chiếc thuyền đã ra xa bờ, cách bờ {{units:vài cây số|nhiều ếch-ta-đơ}}. Sóng đánh vào thuyền rất mạnh, vì gió thổi ngược chiều.

ko.L: 그런데 배는 이미 뭍에서 여러 스타디온 떨어져 있었고, 파도에 시달리고 있었다. 바람이 거슬러 불었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그때 배는 이미 뭍에서 {{units:1.5킬로미터 넘게|여러 스타디온}} 떨어져 있었는데, 맞바람이 불어서 파도에 몹시 시달리고 있었다.
ko.R: 그때 배는 이미 뭍에서 멀리, {{units:1.5킬로미터 넘게|여러 스타디온}} 나가 있었다. 바람이 배 쪽으로 마주 불어서, 파도가 배를 세게 때리고 있었다.

am.L: ጀልባዋም በማዕበሉ እየተንገላታች ከምድር ብዙ ምዕራፍ ርቃ ነበር፤ ነፋሱ ተቃራኒ ነበርና።
am.B: በዚያን ጊዜ ጀልባዋ ከየብስ {{units:ጥቂት ኪሎ ሜትሮች|ብዙ ምዕራፍ}} ርቃ ነበር፤ ነፋሱም ከፊት ለፊታቸው ይነፍስ ስለ ነበር ማዕበሉ ይመታት ነበር።
am.R: በዚህ ጊዜ ጀልባዋ ከየብስ ርቃ ነበር፤ {{units:ጥቂት ኪሎ ሜትሮች|ብዙ ምዕራፍ}} ገብታ ነበር። ነፋሱ በተቃራኒ አቅጣጫ ይነፍስ ስለ ነበር ማዕበሉ ጀልባዋን በኃይል ይመታት ነበር።

decisions.choice: already many stadia away from the land, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: already in the middle of the sea, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "was already in the middle of the sea", as Mark 6:47 has it. The SBLGNT follows other early witnesses with "many stadia away from the land". Both mean the boat was far out on the lake. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: many stadia: a mile or more
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 600 feet (185 meters). Matthew gives no number. John 6:19 says the disciples had rowed twenty-five or thirty stadia, three miles or more.

decisions.choice: battered: tormented, harassed
decisions.reason: The verb means to torment, as of the suffering servant in 8:6. Here the waves torment the boat.

decisions.choice: the wind was against it: a headwind
decisions.reason: The wind blew against the direction they were trying to go, so they made little progress all night.

decisions.choice: {{units:a mile or more|many stadia}}
decisions.reason: The stadion means nothing to most readers, so Balanced and Readable give a distance in miles by default, and the units setting shows the original measure. Literal keeps the ancient unit.

decisions.choice: {{units:dos kilómetros o más|muchos estadios}}
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 185 meters, so "many stadia" is a mile or more (meaning decision m2). Spanish readers measure in kilometers, as at John 6:19, so that is the default, with the original measure as the alternative; the English default is miles. Literal keeps the stadia.

decisions.choice: "plus d’un kilomètre et demi" by default; "de nombreux stades" as the Measures alternative
decisions.reason: French defaults to metric where English uses US units, as at John 6:19. A stadion was about 185 metres, so "many stadia" is at least a kilometre and a half; the figure stays loose, as the Greek is. Literal keeps the unit.

decisions.choice: {{units:kilomita mbili au zaidi|stadia nyingi}}
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 185 metres, so "many stadia" is a mile or more (meaning decision m2). Swahili-speaking countries measure in kilometres, so that is the default, with the original measure as the alternative, as at John 6:19; the English default is miles. Literal keeps the stadia.

decisions.choice: {{units:vài cây số|nhiều ếch-ta-đơ}} (B, R); "nhiều ếch-ta-đơ" (L)
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese units setting gives metric measures by default and the original unit as the alternative (style guide, section 7), where the English gives US miles; "ếch-ta-đơ" is the transliteration used in John 6:19. Literal keeps the Greek unit.

decisions.choice: "bị sóng đánh vùi dập" (L); "bị sóng đánh dữ dội" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb pictures the boat tormented by the waves (meaning decision); "vùi dập" keeps that picture at Literal, while "hành hạ" would sound odd of a boat.

decisions.choice: "여러 스타디온" (L); {{units:1.5킬로미터 넘게|여러 스타디온}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean uses metric measures by default with the original unit as the alternative (style guide, section 7); Literal keeps the Greek unit. A stadion is about 185 metres, so "many stadia" is more than about one and a half kilometres.

decisions.choice: {{units:ጥቂት ኪሎ ሜትሮች|ብዙ ምዕራፍ}} (B, R); "ብዙ ምዕራፍ" (L)
alternatives: US miles, as the English default
decisions.reason: Amharic readers measure distance in kilometres, so the default is metric and the original "stadia" ("ምዕራፍ", the old Amharic word for the stadion) is the alternative; Literal keeps the original unit. This differs from the English, whose default is US units.

source.text: τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν.

records.literal_gloss: In fourth now watch of the night he came to them walking on the sea.

en.L: And in the fourth watch of the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to them, walking on the sea.
en.B: In the last watch of the night, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came out to them, walking on the water.
en.R: Sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning, Jesus came to them. He was walking on top of the water!

es.L: Y en la cuarta guardia de la noche llegó hasta ellos caminando sobre el mar.
es.B: En la última vigilia de la noche, fue hacia ellos caminando sobre el agua.
es.R: Entre las tres y las seis de la mañana, Jesús llegó adonde estaban ellos. ¡Venía caminando sobre el agua!

fr.L: Et à la quatrième veille de la nuit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint vers eux, en marchant sur la mer.
fr.B: À la dernière veille de la nuit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint vers eux en marchant sur l’eau.
fr.R: Entre trois et six heures du matin, Jésus est venu vers eux. Il marchait sur l’eau !

sw.L: Na katika zamu ya nne ya usiku akawajia, akitembea juu ya bahari.
sw.B: Katika zamu ya mwisho ya usiku, aliwajia akitembea juu ya maji.
sw.R: Kati ya saa tisa usiku na saa kumi na mbili alfajiri, Yesu aliwafikia. Alikuwa akitembea juu ya maji!

vi.L: Và vào canh thứ tư của đêm, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi đến với họ, bước đi trên mặt biển.
vi.B: Gần sáng, vào khoảng canh thứ tư, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt nước đến với họ.
vi.R: Vào khoảng từ ba đến sáu giờ sáng, Đức Giê-xu đến với họ. Ngài đi bộ trên mặt nước!

ko.L: 그리고 밤 넷째 경에 그분이 바다 위를 걸으시며 그들에게 오셨다.
ko.B: 밤 넷째 경, 새벽 무렵에 예수께서 바다 위를 걸어 그들에게 오셨다.
ko.R: 새벽 세 시에서 여섯 시 사이에 예수께서 그들에게 오셨다. 예수께서는 물 위를 걷고 계셨다!

am.L: በአራተኛውም የሌሊት ክፍለ ጊዜ በባሕሩ ላይ እየተራመደ ወደ እነርሱ መጣ።
am.B: በመጨረሻው የሌሊት ክፍለ ጊዜ በውኃው ላይ እየተራመደ ወደ እነርሱ መጣ።
am.R: ሌሊቱ ሊነጋ ሲል፣ ከሌሊቱ በዘጠኝና በአሥራ ሁለት ሰዓት መካከል ኢየሱስ ወደ እነርሱ መጣ። በውኃው ላይ እየተራመደ ነበር!

decisions.choice: the fourth watch of the night: from about three to six in the morning
decisions.reason: The Romans divided the night into four watches. The disciples had struggled against the wind most of the night.

decisions.choice: walking on the sea: what Scripture says God alone does
decisions.reason: God alone treads on the waves of the sea (Job 9:8), and his path went through the sea at the exodus (Psalm 77:20). The disciples are far from land (14:24), so Matthew tells of a walk on the water itself.

decisions.choice: in the last watch of the night (B); sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning (R)
alternatives: in the fourth watch of the night
decisions.reason: Balanced says where the watch falls in the night; Readable gives the time in modern terms.

decisions.choice: the water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "water", since it is the walk on the surface that matters, and "sea" could suggest the open ocean. Literal keeps "sea".

decisions.choice: kati ya saa tisa usiku na saa kumi na mbili alfajiri (R)
alternatives: kati ya saa tisa na saa kumi na mbili asubuhi
decisions.reason: The fourth watch ran from about three to six in the morning (meaning decision m1). Swahili counts the hours from sunrise and sunset, so those times are "saa tisa usiku" to "saa kumi na mbili alfajiri", the same hours the English Readable gives in its own reckoning.

decisions.choice: "canh thứ tư" (L, B), with "gần sáng" (B); "từ ba đến sáu giờ sáng" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:48: the Roman fourth watch ran from about three to six in the morning (meaning decision). "Canh tư" in the traditional Vietnamese five-watch night is a different hour, so Literal and Balanced say "canh thứ tư" and Balanced adds "gần sáng".

decisions.choice: "mặt biển" (L); "mặt nước" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "sea", as Mark 6:48 does; Balanced and Readable say "the water", as the English does, which suits both the lake and the walking.

decisions.choice: "밤 넷째 경" (L, B), with "새벽 무렵" (B); "새벽 세 시에서 여섯 시 사이" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 6:48: "사경" is the fourth of the five watches of the traditional Korean night and would give the wrong hour; "밤 넷째 경" keeps the Roman count of four, Balanced adds that it was the last watch before dawn, and Readable gives the modern time (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "ከሌሊቱ በዘጠኝና በአሥራ ሁለት ሰዓት መካከል" (R)
alternatives: "ከሌሊቱ ሦስት እስከ ስድስት ሰዓት", the Western clock
decisions.reason: The fourth watch ran from about three to six in the morning. Ethiopians count the hours from dawn and dusk, so that span is "nine to twelve at night" on the clock Amharic readers use; Literal and Balanced keep the watch.

source.text: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν.

records.literal_gloss: And the disciples having seen him on the sea walking were troubled, saying, A ghost it is, and from the fear they cried out.

en.L: And when the disciples saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the sea, they were terrified, saying, "It is a ghost!" And they cried out in fear.
en.B: The disciples saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} coming across the water and were thrown into panic. "A ghost!" they cried, and they shouted out in terror.
en.R: The followers saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the water, and they were very scared. They said, "It is a ghost!" They screamed because they were so afraid.

es.L: Y cuando los discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron caminando sobre el mar, se turbaron, diciendo: «¡Es un fantasma!», y de miedo gritaron.
es.B: Los discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron venir sobre el agua y se llenaron de pánico. «¡Un fantasma!», decían, y gritaban aterrados.
es.R: Los seguidores {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron caminando sobre el agua y se asustaron mucho. Decían: «¡Es un fantasma!». Gritaban porque tenían mucho miedo.

fr.L: Et les disciples, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyant marcher sur la mer, furent bouleversés et dirent : « C’est un fantôme ! » Et de peur, ils poussèrent des cris.
fr.B: Les disciples {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} virent avancer sur l’eau et furent pris de panique. « Un fantôme ! » dirent-ils, et ils se mirent à crier de terreur.
fr.R: Les disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont vu marcher sur l’eau, et ils ont eu très peur. Ils ont dit : « C’est un fantôme ! » Ils ont crié tellement ils avaient peur.

sw.L: Lakini wanafunzi, walipomwona juu ya bahari akitembea, wakatetemeka, wakisema, "Ni mzuka!" na kwa sababu ya hofu wakalia kwa sauti.
sw.B: Wanafunzi walimwona akija juu ya maji, wakashikwa na hofu kuu. "Ni mzuka!" wakasema, wakapiga kelele kwa woga.
sw.R: Wanafunzi walimwona akitembea juu ya maji, wakaogopa sana. Wakasema, "Ni mzuka!" Walipiga kelele kwa sababu waliogopa mno.

vi.L: Và khi các môn đồ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt biển, họ hoảng hốt và nói rằng: "Đó là ma!" Và họ kêu thét lên vì sợ hãi.
vi.B: Các môn đồ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt nước thì hoảng loạn. Họ kêu lên: "Ma kìa!" và la thét vì kinh hãi.
vi.R: Các môn đồ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi trên mặt nước, và họ rất sợ. Họ nói: "Đó là ma!" Họ la hét lên vì quá sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그러나 제자들은 그분이 바다 위를 걸으시는 것을 보고 겁에 질려 "유령이다!" 하고 말하였다. 그리고 두려워서 소리를 질렀다.
ko.B: 제자들은 예수께서 바다 위로 걸어오시는 것을 보고 몹시 놀라 허둥대며 "유령이다!" 하고 말했다. 그리고 겁에 질려 소리를 질렀다.
ko.R: 제자들은 예수께서 물 위를 걸어오시는 것을 보았다. 그들은 너무 무서웠다. 그들은 "유령이다!" 하고 말하며 비명을 질렀다.

am.L: ደቀ መዛሙርቱም በባሕሩ ላይ ሲራመድ አይተውት ታወኩ፤ «ምትሐት ነው!» አሉ፤ ከፍርሃታቸውም የተነሣ ጮኹ።
am.B: ደቀ መዛሙርቱ በውኃው ላይ ሲመጣ አይተውት እጅግ ተሸበሩ። «ምትሐት ነው!» ብለው በፍርሃት ጮኹ።
am.R: ደቀ መዛሙርቱ በውኃው ላይ ሲራመድ አዩት፤ በጣም ፈሩ። «ምትሐት ነው!» አሉ። በጣም ስለ ፈሩ ጮኹ።

decisions.choice: ghost: an apparition, a phantom
alternatives: the spirit of a dead person only
decisions.reason: The word means something seen that is not real flesh. The disciples think they see a spirit on the water at night.

decisions.choice: were terrified: were shaken, thrown into confusion
decisions.reason: The verb means to be stirred up or deeply disturbed, as Herod was in 2:3.

decisions.choice: coming across the water
decisions.reason: Balanced varies the wording after 14:25; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: mzuka
decisions.reason: The Greek word is an apparition, a phantom (meaning decision m1). "Mzuka" is a ghost that appears to people; "kivuli" is first of all a shadow, and "mzimu" the spirit of an ancestor.

decisions.choice: "ma" for the ghost
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:49: the plain everyday word for an apparition.

source.text: εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι· μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

records.literal_gloss: Immediately now spoke to them Jesus saying, Take courage, I am; not be afraid.

en.L: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Take courage; I am [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}]; do not be afraid."
en.B: Jesus spoke to them at once: "Be brave! It is I. There is nothing to fear."
en.R: Right away Jesus spoke to them. "Be brave!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "It is me, Jesus. Do not be afraid."

es.L: Y al instante les habló Jesús, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} valor, yo soy; no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}».
es.B: Jesús les habló enseguida: «¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} valor! Soy yo. No hay nada que temer».
es.R: En ese mismo momento Jesús les habló. «¡{{plural_you:Anímense|Animaos}}!», les dijo. «Soy yo, Jesús. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo».

fr.L: Mais aussitôt Jésus leur parla, en disant : « Prenez courage ; c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; n’ayez pas peur. »
fr.B: Jésus leur parla aussitôt : « Courage ! C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Vous n’avez rien à craindre. »
fr.R: Tout de suite, Jésus leur a parlé. « Soyez courageux ! a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit. C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, Jésus. N’ayez pas peur. »

sw.L: Lakini mara moja Yesu alizungumza nao, akisema, "Jipeni ujasiri; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye; msiendelee kuogopa."
sw.B: Yesu akasema nao mara moja, "Kuweni jasiri! Ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Hakuna cha kuogopa."
sw.R: Papo hapo Yesu akasema nao. "Kuweni jasiri!" akawaambia. "Ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, Yesu. Msiogope."

vi.L: Nhưng lập tức Đức Giê-xu nói với họ rằng: "Hãy vững lòng! Ta đây; đừng sợ."
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu liền nói với họ: "Hãy can đảm lên! Ta đây. Đừng sợ nữa."
vi.R: Ngay lập tức, Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy yên tâm! Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đây, Giê-xu đây! Đừng sợ!"

ko.L: 그러나 곧 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "용기를 내어라. 나다. 두려워하지 마라."
ko.B: 예수께서 곧바로 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "용기를 내어라. 나다. 이제 두려워하지 마라."
ko.R: 예수께서 바로 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "힘을 내라! 나다, 예수다. 무서워하지 마라."

am.L: ወዲያውም ኢየሱስ እንዲህ ብሎ ተናገራቸው፦ «በርቱ፤ እኔ ነኝ፤ አትፍሩ።»
am.B: ኢየሱስ ወዲያውኑ እንዲህ ብሎ ተናገራቸው፦ «ጠንክሩ! እኔ ነኝ። የምትፈሩት ነገር የለም።»
am.R: ወዲያው ኢየሱስ ተናገራቸው። «በርቱ!» አላቸው። «እኔ ኢየሱስ ነኝ። አትፍሩ።»

decisions.choice: I am: he tells them who he is, in words that echo the name God gave himself
decisions.reason: In ordinary speech the words mean "it is I". But God spoke of himself as "I am" (Exodus 3:14), and in Isaiah God says "I am he" and tells his people not to fear (Isaiah 43:10; 51:12). Spoken by one who walks on the sea, the words may carry both senses; the plain sense is certain, the echo is likely but not sure.

decisions.choice: take courage: be bold, do not lose heart
decisions.reason: As in 9:2 and 9:22, Jesus speaks courage to people in need.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: stop being afraid
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" tells them to stop the fear they already have (14:26). God and his messengers often say these words when they appear (Genesis 15:1; Isaiah 43:1).

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); It is I (B); It is me, Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "I am". Literal brackets the "he" the plain sense needs; Balanced and Readable say the plain sense in everyday words. Readable adds the name so the plain sense is clear. The footnote gives the bare words, so the echo noted in the meaning decision stays visible.

decisions.choice: yo soy (L); Soy yo (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Soy yo" is the plain Spanish for "it is me", what anyone would call out to frightened men in a boat. Literal keeps "yo soy", still a complete answer in Spanish, with the echo of God's own name (meaning decision m1), as at John 6:20.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}}, {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to all the disciples, so every plural "you" and its verb is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). English has no such choice. The same through the passage.

decisions.choice: "c’est moi" (L), where English Literal has "I am [he]"
decisions.reason: As at Mark 6:50: a bare "je suis" is not a French sentence, and "je le suis" would point back to something said before. "C’est moi" says the plain sense; the echo of God's name is given by the meaning note (m1) and the footnote.

decisions.choice: mimi ndiye (L); Ni mimi (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Mimi ndiye" (I am the one, I am he) keeps the shape of the Greek "I am", with the echo of God's name the meaning decision mentions (m1), as at John 6:20. Balanced and Readable say "Ni mimi" (it is me), what anyone would call out in the dark.

decisions.choice: "Ta đây" (L, B); "Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đây, Giê-xu đây" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:50 and John 6:20: "Ta là" with nothing after it is not a Vietnamese sentence, so every level says "Ta đây" (it is I); the echo of God's name is left to the meaning decision and its footnote. Readable adds his name, as the English Readable does. At Literal and Balanced "Ta" begins a sentence and takes no setting span; after "Chính" (R) it takes one.

decisions.choice: "나다" for "I am" at every level; "용기를 내어라" (L, B), "힘을 내라" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 6:50 and John 6:20: "나다" is plain Korean for "it is I" and leaves room for the echo of God's name noted in the meaning decision; "용기를 내어라" keeps the call to courage.

source.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ εἶ, κέλευσόν με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα·

records.literal_gloss: Answering now him Peter said, Lord, if you are, command me to come to you upon the waters.

en.L: And Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Lord, if it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, command me to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on the waters."
en.B: Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, if it is really {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, give me the order to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} over the water."
en.R: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, if it is really {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, tell me to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Tell me to walk on the water."

es.L: Y Pedro, respondiendo, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Señor, si eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, ordéname que vaya hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} sobre las aguas».
es.B: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Señor, si de verdad eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, ordéname que vaya hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} caminando sobre el agua».
es.R: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Señor, si de verdad eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, dime que vaya hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Dime que camine sobre el agua».

fr.L: Et Pierre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit et dit : « Seigneur, si c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, ordonne-moi de venir vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sur les eaux. »
fr.B: Pierre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit : « Seigneur, si c’est vraiment {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, donne-moi l’ordre de venir vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sur l’eau. »
fr.R: Pierre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Seigneur, si c’est vraiment {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, dis-moi de venir vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Dis-moi de marcher sur l’eau. »

sw.L: Naye Petro akamjibu, akisema, "Bwana, kama ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, uniagize nije {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} juu ya maji."
sw.B: Petro akamjibu, "Bwana, ikiwa kweli ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, nipe amri nije {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} juu ya maji."
sw.R: Petro akamwambia, "Bwana, kama kweli ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, niambie nije {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. Niambie nitembee juu ya maji."

vi.L: Và Phi-e-rơ đáp lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Lạy Chúa, nếu là Chúa, xin truyền cho con đi trên mặt nước đến với Chúa."
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, nếu thật là Chúa, xin bảo con đi trên mặt nước đến với Chúa."
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, nếu thật là Chúa, xin bảo con đến với Chúa. Xin bảo con đi trên mặt nước."

ko.L: 그러자 베드로가 그분께 대답하여 말했다. "주님, 주님이시면, 저더러 물 위로 주님께 오라고 명령하십시오."
ko.B: 베드로가 예수께 말했다. "주님, 정말 주님이시면, 저더러 물 위로 걸어서 주님께 오라고 명령해 주십시오."
ko.R: 베드로가 예수께 말했다. "주님, 정말 주님이시면, 저에게 주님께로 오라고 말씀해 주십시오. 물 위로 걸어오라고 말씀해 주십시오."

am.L: ጴጥሮስም መልሶ እንዲህ አለው፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ አንተ ከሆንክ በውኆቹ ላይ ወደ አንተ እንድመጣ እዘዘኝ።»
am.B: ጴጥሮስም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰለት፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ በእርግጥ አንተ ከሆንክ በውኃው ላይ ወደ አንተ እንድመጣ ትእዛዝ ስጠኝ።»
am.R: ጴጥሮስም እንዲህ አለው፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ በእርግጥ አንተ ከሆንክ ወደ አንተ እንድመጣ ንገረኝ። በውኃው ላይ እንድራመድ ንገረኝ።»

decisions.choice: Lord: an address of faith
decisions.reason: As in 8:25, the disciples call Jesus Lord when they turn to him for help and trust his power.

decisions.choice: if it is you: Peter wants to be sure, and asks for a word he can act on
alternatives: since it is you, with no doubt at all
decisions.reason: Peter answers Jesus's "it is I" by asking for a command. His words may hold some doubt, or simply eagerness to go to Jesus; the sense of the condition is open.

decisions.choice: command me to come: only Jesus's word can make it possible
decisions.reason: Peter does not ask to walk on his own; he asks Jesus to call him. He trusts the power of Jesus's command, as the centurion did (8:8).

decisions.choice: really
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "really" to show that Peter wants to be sure who it is.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa", "Chúa" for "you" and "con" for "me" in Peter's words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The settled Matthew form for disciples who call Jesus Lord (as in 8:25); "Chúa" is a noun of address and takes no setting span, although the English "you" has one.

decisions.choice: "주님" for kyrie and again for "you"; Peter speaks in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: The disciples address Jesus as "주님" in the Korean Matthew (8:21, 8:25); Korean does not call a respected person "you", so "주님" stands for the pronoun and is not bracketed in Literal.

decisions.choice: "ጌታ ሆይ" and the familiar "አንተ" when the disciples speak to Jesus
decisions.reason: "ጌታ ሆይ" is the vocative of "ጌታ" and fits a cry of faith; disciples address Jesus with "አንተ", the Bible's familiar address, as the style guide sets for the whole book.

decisions.choice: come: the command Peter asked for
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the one-word command Peter asked for (14:28). It also echoes his call to follow him (4:19).

source.text: καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα καὶ ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone down from the boat Peter walked upon the waters and came to Jesus.

en.L: And going down from the boat, Peter walked on the waters and came toward Jesus.
en.B: So Peter climbed down out of the boat, stepped onto the water, and walked toward Jesus.
en.R: So Peter got out of the boat. He walked on top of the water and went toward Jesus.

es.L: Y bajando de la barca, Pedro caminó sobre las aguas y fue hacia Jesús.
es.B: Pedro bajó entonces de la barca, puso los pies sobre el agua y caminó hacia Jesús.
es.R: Entonces Pedro salió de la barca. Caminó sobre el agua y fue hacia Jesús.

fr.L: Et descendant de la barque, Pierre marcha sur les eaux et vint vers Jésus.
fr.B: Pierre descendit donc de la barque, posa le pied sur l’eau et marcha vers Jésus.
fr.R: Alors Pierre est sorti du bateau. Il a marché sur l’eau et il est allé vers Jésus.

sw.L: Na akiisha kushuka kutoka mashuani, Petro akatembea juu ya maji, akaja kuelekea kwa Yesu.
sw.B: Basi Petro alishuka kutoka mashuani, akakanyaga juu ya maji, akatembea kuelekea kwa Yesu.
sw.R: Basi Petro akatoka mashuani. Akatembea juu ya maji, akaenda kuelekea kwa Yesu.

vi.L: Và Phi-e-rơ bước xuống khỏi thuyền, đi trên mặt nước và đến với Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Vậy Phi-e-rơ bước ra khỏi thuyền, đi trên mặt nước, tiến về phía Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Vậy Phi-e-rơ ra khỏi thuyền. Ông đi trên mặt nước và tiến về phía Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 베드로가 배에서 내려가 물 위를 걸어 예수를 향하여 갔다.
ko.B: 베드로는 배에서 내려 물 위로 발을 내딛고 예수 쪽으로 걸어갔다.
ko.R: 그래서 베드로는 배에서 내렸다. 그리고 물 위를 걸어서 예수 쪽으로 갔다.

am.L: ጴጥሮስም ከጀልባዋ ወርዶ በውኆቹ ላይ ተራመደ፤ ወደ ኢየሱስም መጣ።
am.B: ስለዚህ ጴጥሮስ ከጀልባዋ ወርዶ በውኃው ላይ ረገጠ፤ ወደ ኢየሱስም ተራመደ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ጴጥሮስ ከጀልባዋ ወጣ። በውኃው ላይ ተራምዶ ወደ ኢየሱስ ሄደ።

decisions.choice: and came toward Jesus, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: to come to Jesus, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "walked on the waters to come to Jesus", which says Peter set out to reach him. The SBLGNT reads "and came". Either way, Peter began to sink before he reached Jesus (14:30-31). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: came toward Jesus: went toward him, not reaching him
alternatives: came all the way to Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter begins to sink and Jesus has to reach out to him (14:30-31), so the verb means that he went toward Jesus.

decisions.choice: came toward (L); walked toward (B); went toward (R)
decisions.reason: Every level says "toward", as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: "đến với" (L); "tiến về phía" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "came toward" does not say he reached Jesus (meaning decision); "tiến về phía" (made toward) keeps that open, and Literal keeps the plain verb.

decisions.choice: "예수를 향하여 갔다" (L); "예수 쪽으로" (B, R)
decisions.reason: He went toward Jesus without reaching him (meaning decision); "께로 갔다" would suggest he arrived, while "향하여" and "쪽으로" say only the direction.

source.text: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη, καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων· Κύριε, σῶσόν με.

records.literal_gloss: Seeing now the wind strong he was afraid, and having begun to sink he cried out saying, Lord, save me.

en.L: But seeing the strong wind, he became afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, "Lord, save me!"
en.B: But when he noticed how strong the wind was, fear took hold of him. He started to go under, and he shouted, "Lord, save me!"
en.R: But Peter saw how strong the wind was, and he became afraid. He began to sink into the water. He shouted, "Lord, save me!"

es.L: Mas al ver lo fuerte que era el viento, se atemorizó, y cuando empezaba a hundirse, clamó diciendo: «¡Señor, sálvame!».
es.B: Pero cuando se dio cuenta de la fuerza del viento, el miedo se apoderó de él. Empezó a hundirse y gritó: «¡Señor, sálvame!».
es.R: Pero Pedro vio lo fuerte que soplaba el viento y le dio miedo. Comenzó a hundirse en el agua. Gritó: «¡Señor, sálvame!».

fr.L: Mais voyant le vent fort, il eut peur, et commençant à s’enfoncer, il s’écria : « Seigneur, sauve-moi ! »
fr.B: Mais quand il remarqua la force du vent, la peur le saisit. Il commença à couler, et il cria : « Seigneur, sauve-moi ! »
fr.R: Mais Pierre a vu que le vent était très fort, et il a eu peur. Il a commencé à s’enfoncer dans l’eau. Il a crié : « Seigneur, sauve-moi ! »

sw.L: Lakini akiutazama upepo mkali, aliingiwa na hofu, na akianza kuzama, akalia kwa sauti kubwa, akisema, "Bwana, niokoe!"
sw.B: Lakini alipoona jinsi upepo ulivyokuwa mkali, hofu ikamshika. Akaanza kuzama, akapaza sauti, "Bwana, niokoe!"
sw.R: Lakini Petro aliona jinsi upepo ulivyokuwa na nguvu, akaogopa. Akaanza kuzama majini. Akapiga kelele, "Bwana, niokoe!"

vi.L: Nhưng thấy gió mạnh, ông sợ hãi, và bắt đầu chìm xuống, ông kêu lên rằng: "Lạy Chúa, xin cứu con!"
vi.B: Nhưng khi thấy gió thổi mạnh, ông sợ hãi. Ông bắt đầu chìm xuống và kêu lên: "Lạy Chúa, xin cứu con!"
vi.R: Nhưng Phi-e-rơ thấy gió thổi rất mạnh, và ông sợ. Ông bắt đầu chìm xuống nước. Ông kêu lớn: "Lạy Chúa, xin cứu con!"

ko.L: 그러나 그는 강한 바람을 보고 두려워졌다. 그리고 물에 빠져 들어가기 시작하자 소리 질러 말했다. "주님, 저를 구원해 주십시오!"
ko.B: 그러나 그는 바람이 거센 것을 보자 두려워졌다. 그리고 물에 빠져 들어가기 시작하자 소리쳤다. "주님, 저를 구해 주십시오!"
ko.R: 그런데 베드로는 바람이 아주 센 것을 보고 무서워졌다. 그러자 물속으로 가라앉기 시작했다. 베드로가 소리쳤다. "주님, 저를 살려 주십시오!"

am.L: ነገር ግን ብርቱውን ነፋስ አይቶ ፈራ፤ መስጠምም ጀምሮ እንዲህ እያለ ጮኸ፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ አድነኝ!»
am.B: ነገር ግን ነፋሱ ምን ያህል ብርቱ እንደ ሆነ ባየ ጊዜ ፍርሃት ያዘው። መስጠም ጀመረ፤ እንዲህም ብሎ ጮኸ፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ አድነኝ!»
am.R: ጴጥሮስ ግን ነፋሱ ምን ያህል ኃይለኛ እንደ ሆነ አየ፤ ፈራም። በውኃው ውስጥ መስጠም ጀመረ። እርሱም እንዲህ ብሎ ጮኸ፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ አድነኝ!»

decisions.choice: the strong wind, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the wind, without "strong", in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read only "seeing the wind". Many others add "strong", which the SBLGNT prints. The sense is little changed: Peter looked at the wind and lost his nerve. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: seeing the wind he was afraid: he turned his eyes from Jesus to the danger
decisions.reason: Peter walked while he trusted Jesus's word. When he looked at the wind, fear took hold, and he began to sink. Jesus names the cause as doubt (14:31).

decisions.choice: Lord, save me: a cry for rescue in the words of prayer
decisions.reason: The cry echoes the Psalms' calls to God from deep waters (Psalm 69:2-3; 144:7), as at 8:25.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa, xin cứu con!"
decisions.reason: Peter's cry is in the words of prayer (meaning decision), as the disciples' "Lạy Chúa, xin cứu chúng con" in 8:25; "xin" keeps it a plea.

decisions.choice: "구원해 주십시오" (L); "구해 주십시오" (B); "살려 주십시오" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 8:25: the cry uses the words of prayer (meaning decision); Literal keeps the weight of "구원", the other levels the plain cry for rescue.

source.text: εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὀλιγόπιστε, εἰς τί ἐδίστασας;

records.literal_gloss: Immediately now Jesus having stretched out the hand took hold of him and says to him, Of little faith, for why did you doubt?

en.L: And immediately Jesus stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and took hold of him, and says to him, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"
en.B: Jesus at once put out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and took hold of him. "You have so little faith," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him. "Why did you doubt?"
en.R: Right away Jesus reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and caught Peter. Jesus said to him, "Your faith is so small! Why did you doubt?"

es.L: Al instante Jesús extendió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y lo sujetó, y le dice: «Oh tú, de poca fe, ¿para qué dudaste?».
es.B: Jesús extendió enseguida {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y lo sostuvo. «¡Qué poca fe tienes!», le dijo. «¿Por qué dudaste?».
es.R: Al momento Jesús extendió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y agarró a Pedro. Le dijo: «¡Tu fe es muy pequeña! ¿Por qué dudaste?».

fr.L: Et aussitôt Jésus, étendant la main, le saisit, et lui dit : « Homme de peu de foi, pourquoi as-tu douté ? »
fr.B: Jésus tendit aussitôt la main et le saisit. « Tu as si peu de foi ! lui dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}. Pourquoi as-tu douté ? »
fr.R: Tout de suite, Jésus a tendu la main et a attrapé Pierre. Jésus lui a dit : « Ta foi est si petite ! Pourquoi as-tu douté ? »

sw.L: Mara moja Yesu, akiunyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamkamata, na anamwambia, "Wewe mwenye imani ndogo, ulisita kwa ajili ya nini?"
sw.B: Yesu alinyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mara moja, akamshika. "Imani yako ni ndogo mno," akamwambia. "Kwa nini ulisita?"
sw.R: Papo hapo Yesu alinyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamshika Petro. Yesu akamwambia, "Imani yako ni ndogo sana! Kwa nini ulikuwa na shaka?"

vi.L: Lập tức Đức Giê-xu đưa tay ra nắm lấy ông, và nói với ông: "Hỡi người ít đức tin, sao con nghi ngờ?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu liền đưa tay ra nắm lấy ông và nói: "Đức tin của con ít quá! Sao con lại nghi ngờ?"
vi.R: Ngay lập tức, Đức Giê-xu đưa tay ra nắm lấy Phi-e-rơ. Ngài nói với ông: "Đức tin của con thật nhỏ bé! Tại sao con lại nghi ngờ?"

ko.L: 곧 예수께서 손을 내밀어 그를 붙잡으시고 그에게 말씀하신다. "믿음이 작은 사람아, 왜 의심하였느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 곧바로 손을 내밀어 그를 붙잡으시고 말씀하셨다. "믿음이 작은 사람아, 왜 의심하였느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 바로 손을 뻗어 베드로를 붙잡으셨다. 그리고 그에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 믿음이 너무 작구나! 왜 의심하였느냐?"

am.L: ወዲያውም ኢየሱስ እጁን ዘርግቶ ያዘው፤ እንዲህም ይለዋል፦ «አንተ እምነትህ ትንሽ የሆነ፣ ለምን ተጠራጠርክ?»
am.B: ኢየሱስ ወዲያውኑ እጁን ዘርግቶ ያዘው። «እምነትህ እንዴት ትንሽ ነው!» አለው። «ለምን ተጠራጠርክ?»
am.R: ወዲያው ኢየሱስ እጁን ዘርግቶ ጴጥሮስን ያዘው። ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አለው፦ «እምነትህ በጣም ትንሽ ነው! ለምን ተጠራጠርክ?»

decisions.choice: of little faith: having real but weak trust
decisions.reason: As in 6:30 and 8:26, the word rebukes a disciple whose faith is real but gives way. Peter's faith carried him onto the water, and then failed.

decisions.choice: doubt: waver, be of two minds
decisions.reason: The verb means to hesitate between two ways. Matthew uses it again only in 28:17, of some who worshiped the risen Jesus.

decisions.choice: stretched out his hand and took hold of him: God's hand rescues from the waters
decisions.reason: A psalm asks God to reach down his hand from above and pull the psalmist out of deep waters (Psalm 144:7; compare 18:17). Jesus does what the psalm asks of God.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: You have so little faith (B); Your faith is so small (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the one-word address into a short statement, as at 6:30 and 8:26.

decisions.choice: ¿para qué dudaste? (L); ¿Por qué dudaste? (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek asks "for what" (into what) Peter doubted. Spanish "para qué" keeps that shape at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary "por qué", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "la main", with no possessive
decisions.reason: French says "étendre la main" with the article, as the Greek does, so there is no pronoun to carry the deity_pronoun span that English has on "his hand".

decisions.choice: ulisita (L, B); ulikuwa na shaka (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is to waver, to be of two minds (meaning decision m2). "Kusita" is to hesitate between two ways; Readable uses the everyday "kuwa na shaka".

decisions.choice: "người ít đức tin" (L); "Đức tin của con ít quá" (B); "Đức tin của con thật nhỏ bé" (R)
decisions.reason: The one Greek word "little-faith", said with the key term "đức tin" at every level, as in 8:26 (to one person here, so "con"). Literal keeps the vocative "Hỡi".

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L) for the present "says"
decisions.reason: Matthew tells this in the present tense; Literal keeps it by leaving out the past marker, as in Mark. Balanced and Readable tell it in the past from the context.

decisions.choice: "믿음이 작은 사람아" (L, B); "너는 믿음이 너무 작구나!" (R); present "말씀하신다" (L)
decisions.reason: The Korean Matthew's settled form (6:30, 8:26), here in the singular for Peter, with the key term "믿음" at every level. Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: "አንተ እምነትህ ትንሽ የሆነ" (L); "እምነትህ እንዴት ትንሽ ነው!" (B); "እምነትህ በጣም ትንሽ ነው!" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's word means faith that is real but small, not faith that is missing; "lacking faith" would say he had none. Used for "you of little faith" through Matthew.

source.text: καὶ ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone up they into the boat ceased the wind.

en.L: And when they had gone up into the boat, the wind stopped.
en.B: As soon as the two of them had climbed into the boat, the wind dropped.
en.R: Jesus and Peter got into the boat, and the wind stopped blowing.

es.L: Y habiendo subido ellos a la barca, amainó el viento.
es.B: En cuanto los dos subieron a la barca, el viento se calmó.
es.R: Jesús y Pedro subieron a la barca, y el viento dejó de soplar.

fr.L: Et quand ils furent montés dans la barque, le vent cessa.
fr.B: Dès qu’ils furent montés tous les deux dans la barque, le vent tomba.
fr.R: Jésus et Pierre sont montés dans le bateau, et le vent s’est arrêté de souffler.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wamepanda katika mashua, upepo ukatulia.
sw.B: Mara wawili hao walipoingia mashuani, upepo ukapungua.
sw.R: Yesu na Petro wakaingia mashuani, na upepo ukaacha kuvuma.

vi.L: Và khi họ đã lên thuyền, gió ngừng lại.
vi.B: Khi hai người vừa lên thuyền thì gió lặng.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và Phi-e-rơ leo lên thuyền, và gió ngừng thổi.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 배에 오르자, 바람이 그쳤다.
ko.B: 예수께서 베드로와 함께 배에 오르시자, 바람이 잔잔해졌다.
ko.R: 예수께서 베드로와 함께 배에 오르셨다. 그러자 바람이 멈추었다.

am.L: እነርሱም ወደ ጀልባዋ በወጡ ጊዜ ነፋሱ ጸጥ አለ።
am.B: ሁለቱም ወደ ጀልባዋ እንደ ወጡ ነፋሱ ቆመ።
am.R: ኢየሱስና ጴጥሮስ ወደ ጀልባዋ ገቡ፤ ነፋሱም ቆመ።

decisions.choice: they: Jesus and Peter
decisions.reason: The other disciples were already in the boat; the two on the water climb in.

decisions.choice: ceased: grew tired, died down
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow weary or stop. The wind falls still once Jesus is in the boat, as in 8:26.

decisions.choice: the two of them (B); Jesus and Peter (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who climbed into the boat.

decisions.choice: "예수께서 베드로와 함께" for "the two of them"
decisions.reason: With a joint subject Korean must choose whether the verb is honorific; as in the Korean Mark 8:27, making Jesus the subject "with" Peter keeps the honorific for Jesus alone. Literal keeps the bare "그들이".

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς εἶ.

records.literal_gloss: Those then in the boat worshiped him saying, Truly of God Son you are.

en.L: And those in the boat worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Truly {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God."
en.B: Everyone in the boat fell down and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "You really are the Son of God!" they said.
en.R: Then everyone in the boat worshiped Jesus. They said, "It is true! You are the Son of God!"

es.L: Y los que [estaban] en la barca {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} adoraron, diciendo: «De verdad, Hijo de Dios eres».
es.B: Todos los que estaban en la barca se postraron y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} adoraron. «¡Realmente {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el Hijo de Dios!», decían.
es.R: Entonces todos los que estaban en la barca adoraron a Jesús. Decían: «¡Es verdad! ¡Tú eres el Hijo de Dios!».

fr.L: Et ceux qui étaient dans la barque {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adorèrent, en disant : « Vraiment, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es [le] Fils de Dieu. »
fr.B: Tous ceux qui étaient dans la barque se prosternèrent devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. « Tu es vraiment le Fils de Dieu ! » dirent-ils.
fr.R: Alors tous ceux qui étaient dans le bateau ont adoré Jésus. Ils ont dit : « C’est vrai ! Tu es le Fils de Dieu ! »

sw.L: Na wale [waliokuwa] mashuani wakamwabudu, wakisema, "Kweli {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu."
sw.B: Wote waliokuwa mashuani walianguka, wakamwabudu. "Kwa kweli {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu!" wakasema.
sw.R: Kisha wote waliokuwa mashuani wakamwabudu Yesu. Wakasema, "Ni kweli! Wewe ni Mwana wa Mungu!"

vi.L: Và những người ở trong thuyền thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói rằng: "Thầy thật là Con Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Những người ở trong thuyền đều sấp mình thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Thầy thật là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"
vi.R: Rồi mọi người trong thuyền thờ lạy Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói: "Thật vậy! Thầy là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"

ko.L: 그러자 배 안에 있던 사람들이 그분께 경배하며 말했다. "참으로 주님은 하나님의 아들이십니다."
ko.B: 배 안에 있던 사람들은 예수께 경배하며 말했다. "주님은 참으로 하나님의 아들이십니다!"
ko.R: 그러자 배 안에 있던 사람들이 모두 예수께 엎드려 경배했다. 그들이 말했다. "정말입니다! 주님은 하나님의 아들이십니다!"

am.L: በጀልባዋ የነበሩትም ሰገዱለት፤ እንዲህም አሉ፦ «በእውነት አንተ የእግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ።»
am.B: በጀልባዋ የነበሩት ሁሉ ወድቀው ሰገዱለት። «አንተ በእርግጥ የእግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ!» አሉ።
am.R: ከዚያም በጀልባዋ የነበሩት ሁሉ ለኢየሱስ ሰገዱ። እንዲህም አሉ፦ «እውነት ነው! አንተ የእግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ!»

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down before him in worship
alternatives: paid him respect as to a great man
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone. Matthew uses it of the magi (2:11) and of worship due to God alone (4:10). After what they have seen, the disciples give Jesus the honor that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: Truly you are the Son of God: the first time the disciples confess Jesus as God's Son
alternatives: a son of God, a godlike man
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article, but the title is the one God spoke at Jesus's baptism (3:17) and the tempter and demons used (4:3, 6; 8:29). Here the disciples say it in worship. Peter will confess it again (16:16), and a centurion at the cross (27:54).

decisions.choice: those in the boat: the disciples, perhaps with others
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "those in the boat". The disciples are meant, and no one else is mentioned.

decisions.choice: [the] Son of God
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the article the Greek leaves out, as at 4:3.

decisions.choice: Hijo de Dios eres (L)
decisions.reason: Spanish can put the title before the verb, as the Greek does, so Literal keeps the stress on "Son of God"; with that order Spanish needs no supplied article.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" in the disciples' confession, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: With no "Lord" in the Greek, the disciples speak to Jesus as "Thầy", their usual address, as Peter does in Mark 8:29 and Matthew 16:16; it is a noun of address and takes no setting span.

decisions.choice: "thờ lạy"; "sấp mình thờ lạy" (B)
decisions.reason: The settled Matthew word for this verb (2:2); Balanced adds the bowing down the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "경배하다" (L, B); "엎드려 경배하다" (R); "주님은 ... 하나님의 아들이십니다" for "you are"
decisions.reason: As settled in the Korean Matthew 2: they bow down in worship (meaning decision). Korean supplies "주님" where Greek says "you", as the disciples address Jesus throughout the Korean Matthew.

decisions.choice: "ሰገዱለት" (bowed down in worship)
decisions.reason: "ሰገደ" says both the bowing down and the worship that the Greek verb means; "አመለከ" names worship of a god without the act.

source.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς Γεννησαρέτ.

records.literal_gloss: And having crossed over they came to the land into Gennesaret.

en.L: And having crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
en.B: After crossing the lake, they came ashore at Gennesaret.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed the lake and landed at a place called Gennesaret.

es.L: Y habiendo cruzado, llegaron a tierra en Genesaret.
es.B: Después de cruzar el lago, desembarcaron en Genesaret.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores cruzaron el lago y llegaron a un lugar llamado Genesaret.

fr.L: Et ayant traversé, ils arrivèrent à terre à Génésareth.
fr.B: Après avoir traversé le lac, ils accostèrent à Génésareth.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont traversé le lac et ils sont arrivés à un endroit appelé Génésareth.

sw.L: Na baada ya kuvuka, walikuja nchi kavu huko Genesareti.
sw.B: Baada ya kuvuka ziwa, walishuka pwani huko Genesareti.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walivuka ziwa, wakafika mahali panapoitwa Genesareti.

vi.L: Và sau khi qua [bờ bên kia], họ đến đất Ghê-nê-xa-rét.
vi.B: Qua bên kia biển rồi, họ cập bờ ở vùng Ghê-nê-xa-rét.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ qua bên kia hồ, và họ lên bờ ở một nơi gọi là vùng Ghê-nê-xa-rét.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 건너가서 게네사렛 땅에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들과 함께 호수를 건너 게네사렛이라는 곳에 이르셨다.

am.B: ሐይቁን ተሻግረው ጌንሴሬጥ ላይ ወደ የብስ ወጡ።
am.R: ኢየሱስና ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ሐይቁን ተሻግረው ጌንሴሬጥ ወደሚባል ስፍራ ደረሱ።

decisions.choice: Gennesaret: a fertile plain on the northwest shore of the lake of Galilee
alternatives: a town on the eastern shore
decisions.reason: The plain of Gennesaret lay south of Capernaum. The lake itself was sometimes called by the same name (Luke 5:1).

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; a place called
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Readable says who crossed and that Gennesaret is a place.

decisions.choice: "Génésareth"
decisions.reason: The usual French spelling, as at Mark 6:53.

decisions.choice: "Ghê-nê-xa-rét"; "vùng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:53: Gennesaret is a plain by the lake (meaning decision), so Vietnamese says "vùng" (region).

decisions.choice: "게네사렛"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant form, as in the Korean Mark 6:53.

source.text: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην, καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ· καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having recognized him the men of the place that sent into all the surrounding region that and brought to him all those sick being, \v 36 and they were begging him that only they might touch the fringe of the garment of him; and as many as touched were made completely well.

en.L: And when the {{gender:people|men}} of that place recognized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they sent into all that surrounding region and brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all who were sick, \v 36 and they kept begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that they might only touch the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment; and as many as touched [it] were made completely well.
en.B: The people of that place knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, and they sent messengers all through the region around. They brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everyone who was ill \v 36 and pleaded to be allowed simply to touch the tassel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak. Every one of them who touched it was fully healed.
en.R: The people who lived there knew who Jesus was. So they sent messages to all the places around. People brought everyone who was sick to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 36 They begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to let the sick people touch just the edge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes. And every sick person who touched it was healed.

es.L: Y cuando {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de aquel lugar {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} reconocieron, mandaron [aviso] por toda aquella comarca y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} llevaron a todos los que se hallaban mal, \v 36 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaban que tan solo pudieran tocar el fleco de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto; y todos cuantos [lo] tocaron fueron sanados por completo.
es.B: La gente de aquel lugar supo quién era y mandó recado por toda la región de alrededor. Le trajeron a todos los que estaban enfermos \v 36 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaban que los dejara tocar aunque fuera la borla de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto. Todos los que la tocaron quedaron completamente sanos.
es.R: La gente que vivía allí supo quién era Jesús. Por eso enviaron mensajes a todos los lugares de alrededor. Le llevaron a todos los enfermos. \v 36 Le rogaban que dejara a los enfermos tocar aunque fuera la orilla de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa. Y todos los enfermos que la tocaron quedaron sanos.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:gens|hommes}} de ce lieu, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant reconnu, envoyèrent [des messagers] dans toute cette région environnante, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amenèrent tous ceux qui allaient mal, \v 36 et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliaient de pouvoir seulement toucher la frange de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} vêtement ; et tous ceux qui [la] touchèrent furent complètement guéris.
fr.B: Les gens de l’endroit {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnurent, et ils envoyèrent des messagers dans toute la région alentour. On {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amena tous les malades, \v 36 et on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliait de les laisser seulement toucher la frange de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau. Tous ceux qui la touchèrent furent pleinement guéris.
fr.R: Les gens qui habitaient là ont su que c’était Jésus. Alors ils ont envoyé des messages dans tous les endroits autour. Les gens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont amené tous les malades. \v 36 Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliaient de laisser les malades toucher juste le bord de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau. Et tous les malades qui l’ont touché ont été guéris.

sw.L: Na wakazi wa mahali pale walipomtambua, wakapeleka ujumbe katika eneo lote lile la jirani, wakamletea wote waliokuwa wakiugua, \v 36 na wakaendelea kumwomba ili wapate kugusa tu pindo la joho {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}; na wote walioligusa wakaponywa kikamilifu.
sw.B: Watu wa mahali pale walimtambua, wakatuma wajumbe katika eneo lote la jirani. Wakamletea kila mtu aliyekuwa mgonjwa, \v 36 wakamsihi awaruhusu waguse tu kishada cha joho {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. Kila aliyekigusa alipona kabisa.
sw.R: Watu walioishi pale walimtambua Yesu. Basi wakatuma habari mahali pote palipowazunguka. Watu wakamletea wagonjwa wote. \v 36 Wakamwomba awaruhusu wagonjwa waguse ukingo wa nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} tu. Na kila mgonjwa aliyeugusa alipona.

vi.L: Và khi người ở nơi ấy nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ sai [người] đi khắp cả vùng chung quanh, và đem đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tất cả những người đau ốm, \v 36 và họ nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ chỉ được chạm vào tua áo choàng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; và hễ ai chạm vào đều được lành hẳn.
vi.B: Dân ở nơi ấy nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nên họ sai người đi báo tin khắp vùng chung quanh. Họ đem đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mọi người đau ốm, \v 36 và nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ chỉ được chạm vào tua áo choàng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thôi. Ai chạm vào đều được lành hẳn.
vi.R: Dân ở đó nhận ra Đức Giê-xu. Vì vậy, họ sai người báo tin cho mọi nơi chung quanh. Người ta đem tất cả những người bệnh đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 36 Họ nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho người bệnh chỉ được chạm vào mép áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Và ai chạm vào đều được lành bệnh.

ko.L: 그리고 그곳 사람들이 그분을 알아보고 그 주변 온 지역에 [사람을] 보내어, 앓는 사람들을 모두 그분께 데려왔다. \v 36 그리고 그분의 겉옷 술만이라도 만지게 해 달라고 그분께 간청하고 있었다. 그리고 만진 사람은 모두 온전히 나았다.
ko.B: 그곳 사람들은 예수를 알아보고, 그 주변 온 지역에 사람을 보내어 병든 사람을 모두 예수께 데려왔다. \v 36 그리고 예수의 겉옷 술만이라도 만지게 해 달라고 거듭 간청했다. 그것을 만진 사람은 모두 완전히 나았다.
ko.R: 그곳 사람들은 예수를 알아보았다. 그래서 그 근처 모든 곳에 소식을 보냈다. 사람들이 아픈 사람을 모두 예수께 데려왔다. \v 36 그리고 아픈 사람들이 예수의 옷자락만이라도 만지게 해 달라고 예수께 빌었다. 옷자락을 만진 사람은 모두 병이 나았다.

am.L: የዚያም ስፍራ {{gender:ሰዎች|ወንዶች}} ባወቁት ጊዜ ወደዚያ ዙሪያ አገር ሁሉ ላኩ፤ ሕመምተኞችንም ሁሉ ወደ እርሱ አመጡ፤ \v 36 የልብሱን ዘርፍ ብቻ እንዲነኩ ይለምኑት ነበር፤ የነኩትም ሁሉ ፈጽመው ዳኑ።
am.B: የዚያ ስፍራ ሰዎች ማን እንደ ሆነ አወቁ፤ በዙሪያው ወዳለው አገር ሁሉ መልእክተኞች ላኩ። የታመሙትንም ሁሉ ወደ እርሱ አመጡ፤ \v 36 የልብሱን ዘርፍ ብቻ እንዲነኩ ይፈቅድላቸው ዘንድ ለመኑት። የነኩትም ሁሉ ፍጹም ተፈወሱ።
am.R: በዚያ የሚኖሩ ሰዎች ኢየሱስ ማን እንደ ሆነ አወቁ። ስለዚህ በዙሪያቸው ወዳሉት ስፍራዎች ሁሉ መልእክት ላኩ። ሰዎችም የታመመውን ሁሉ ወደ እርሱ አመጡ። \v 36 የታመሙት ሰዎች የልብሱን ጫፍ ብቻ እንዲነኩ እንዲፈቅድላቸው ለመኑት። የነካውም የታመመ ሰው ሁሉ ተፈወሰ።

decisions.choice: the men of that place: the people who lived there
decisions.reason: "The men of" a place is a common way of naming its people, as "the men of Nineveh" in 12:41.

decisions.choice: the fringe of his garment: the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels on the corners of their cloaks (Numbers 15:38-39; Deuteronomy 22:12). The people hope for what the woman found in 9:20-22. The word can also mean simply the edge.

decisions.choice: were made completely well: brought safely through, fully healed
decisions.reason: The verb is a strengthened form of the word for "save" used in 9:21-22. It means a complete healing.

decisions.choice: were begging: kept begging, one after another
decisions.reason: The tense pictures request after request as the sick were brought.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: Literal uses the gender setting for the general "men of that place", as at 12:41. Balanced and Readable say "people", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: fringe (L); tassel (B); edge (R)
decisions.reason: As at 9:20: Literal keeps "fringe", Balanced names the tassel, and Readable uses the simpler "edge".

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} (L); la gente (B, R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means the people who lived there (meaning decision m1). As in English, Literal offers the traditional "los hombres" under the setting; "las personas" keeps the plural verb in both forms. Balanced and Readable say "la gente".

decisions.choice: el fleco (L); la borla (B); la orilla (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the word is probably the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision m2, uncertain). Literal says "fleco", Balanced "borla", the tassel itself, and Readable the plain "orilla".

decisions.choice: "la frange" (L, B); "le bord" (R)
decisions.reason: French "frange" already names the tassels at the corners of the cloak, as at Mark 6:56; "houppe" and "gland" would suggest decoration. Readable says "le bord", the simpler word, as the English "edge".

decisions.choice: wakazi (L); watu (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The phrase means the people who lived there (meaning decision m1). "Wakazi" (inhabitants) and "watu" already include men and women; "wanaume" would say males only, so Swahili needs no gender span where the English Literal has one.

decisions.choice: pindo (L); kishada (B); ukingo (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the word is probably the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision m2, uncertain). Literal says "pindo" (fringe), Balanced "kishada", the tassel itself, and Readable the plain "ukingo" (edge).

decisions.choice: "tua áo choàng" (L, B); "mép áo" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 9:20: the fringe is the tassel at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision), "tua"; Readable says the edge of his clothes.

decisions.choice: "người ở nơi ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Người" takes in men and women, so the English gender setting has nothing to choose between in Vietnamese.

decisions.choice: "겉옷 술" (L, B); "옷자락" (R); "온전히 나았다" (L), "완전히 나았다" (B), "병이 나았다" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 9:20: the tassel at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision), with Readable's plainer "옷자락". "그곳 사람들" takes no gender span: Korean "사람" already includes men and women.

decisions.choice: [사람을]
decisions.reason: The Greek "sent" has no object; Korean needs one, and Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ሰዎች|ወንዶች}} (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "men" but means the people of the place; as in English, the inclusive word is the default and the traditional "ወንዶች" the alternative. Balanced and Readable say "ሰዎች", as the English does.
